name: Orla Mabrey
equipment: A battered tavern sign reading 'Northwind Arms' (salvaged from the wreckage)
A letter from her daughter, unopened and creased from handling
features: Fighting Style: Defense (+1 AC while wearing armor — already included in AC calculation)
Second Wind (bonus action, regain 1d10+5 HP, 1/short rest)
Action Surge (take one additional action on your turn, 1/short rest)
Extra Attack (attack twice when taking the Attack action)
Improved Critical (weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20)

Veteran's Instinct (1/short rest, as a reaction when an ally within 5 feet is targeted by an attack, swap places with that ally and become the target of the attack instead. The attack roll is compared against Orla's AC. 'You don't survive thirty years of adventuring without learning to watch your friends' backs.')
Rally the Line (1/long rest, as a bonus action, Orla shouts a battlefield command. All allies within 30 feet gain 8 temporary hit points that last for 1 minute. 'On your feet! We're not done yet!')

Innkeeper's Network (spend 1 hour in any settlement's tavern or inn to gather reliable local intelligence — troop movements, rumors, supply situations, notable visitors. Orla knows every barkeep, serving maid, and stable hand on the Cormorant Coast, and they trust her.)

Sentinel (feat — when a creature within 5 feet attacks someone other than you, use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature; creatures you hit with opportunity attacks have their speed reduced to 0 for the turn; creatures within 5 feet don't gain benefit of Disengage)
Soldier: Military Rank (can invoke former rank among members and veterans of the Iron Vigil to requisition supplies, secure cooperation, or access restricted areas)

Tough as Nails (Orla has survived wounds that should have killed her three times over. When she succeeds on a death saving throw, she can choose to regain 1 HP instead of gaining a success. 1/long rest.)

personality.traits: I call everyone 'kid' regardless of their age — it's equal parts affection and habit. I assess every room I enter for exits, cover positions, and potential threats before I even take my coat off. I cook for the party whether they ask me to or not, and I take personal offense if anyone skips a meal.
personality.ideals: Duty. When you see something wrong, you fix it. When someone needs help, you help them. It's not complicated, and people who make it complicated are usually looking for an excuse to do nothing. I didn't survive thirty years of adventuring to sit in a rocking chair while the world burns.
personality.bonds: My tavern, the Northwind Arms, was more than a business — it was a home for every traveler, exile, and lost soul on the northern Cormorant Coast. The hill giants who destroyed it took something I can never rebuild. My daughter Kella joined the Drowned Hand three years ago, and I don't know if she's a victim or a villain. Finding out is the thing that keeps me up at night.
personality.flaws: I am stubborn to a fault — once I decide something is right, I will not bend, even when compromise would be wiser. I also carry guilt like a stone in my chest: guilt for retiring while the world still needed fighters, guilt for not seeing what my daughter was becoming, guilt for every person who died in my tavern when the giants came. I drink more than I should, though it never affects my fighting.

appearance: Orla Mabrey is a broad-shouldered human woman in her mid-fifties who looks exactly like what she is — a retired adventurer who has been dragged back into the fight. She stands five feet ten inches tall, built solid and powerful rather than lean, with the kind of muscle that comes from decades of swinging a sword followed by years of hauling kegs and chopping firewood. Her face is weathered and lined, with deep crow's feet around sharp brown eyes that miss absolutely nothing. Her hair is iron-gray, cut short and practical, and a vivid scar runs across her left forearm where a bugbear nearly took her hand twenty years ago. Her hands are calloused and scarred — the hands of someone who has built things and broken things in equal measure. She wears her chain mail with the ease of old habit, a battered oak shield on her back marked with the faded symbol of the Iron Vigil — an open hand upon a tower. Her longsword is plain but perfectly maintained, the kind of weapon that values function over flash. She carries herself with the steady, grounded confidence of someone who has seen the worst the world has to offer and decided to keep going anyway. There is warmth in her face when she looks at her companions — a maternal protectiveness that she would deny if confronted with it. Around her neck, hidden under her armor, hangs the medallion of the Iron Vigil. In her belt pouch, always, is a creased and unopened letter from her daughter.
backstory: Orla Mabrey spent thirty years as an adventurer with the Iron Vigil — a holy order dedicated to striking down evil and protecting the innocent across the Cormorant Coast. She was never the flashiest member, never the one the bards wrote songs about. She was the one who held the line when everyone else broke, the one who carried the wounded out, the one who stayed behind to cover the retreat. She rose to the rank of Marshal — a field commander — and led her own squad through campaigns against orc hordes, undead incursions, and a particularly nasty green dragon in the Sedgewaste. She took wounds that would have killed lesser fighters. She buried friends. She kept going. When she finally retired at forty-five, she bought a run-down coaching inn on the road between Wainscross and Weirford and transformed it into the Northwind Arms — a warm, well-defended waystation that became legendary among travelers on the northern Cormorant Coast. She served strong ale, stronger whiskey, and the best venison stew in the region. She listened to travelers' stories and dispensed unsolicited advice. She kept a sword behind the bar and everyone knew it. For ten years, it was the closest thing to peace she had ever known. Then two things happened. First, her daughter Kella — her brilliant, restless, angry daughter — left home and joined the Drowned Hand. The Drowned Hand is a shadowy organization that worships a kraken named Vaskoloth and operates through espionage, manipulation, and maritime piracy. Orla does not know if Kella was recruited, coerced, or went willingly. Kella's last letter — which Orla has never been able to bring herself to open — arrived three months before the giants attacked. Second, a raiding party of hill giants descended on the Northwind Arms during the harvest festival. Orla fought them with a kitchen knife and a broken table leg while her guests fled. She killed one — drove the knife into its eye — but the others destroyed everything. The tavern, the stables, the garden she had spent a decade cultivating. Three guests who could not escape in time were crushed. Orla pulled their bodies from the rubble herself. She buried them behind the ruins, retrieved her old armor and sword from the cellar where she had stored them, and started walking south. She is not adventuring again because she wants to. She is adventuring because the world gave her no choice. She carries the guilt of retirement — the years she spent pouring ale while the threats were building — and she is determined to make them count for something. She joined the party because they are heading into the heart of the giant crisis, and she knows the terrain, the politics, and the cost of doing nothing.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Orla is the party's backbone — the steady, unshakable presence who keeps everyone grounded when things go sideways. Play her as gruff, warm, and relentlessly practical. She does not waste words, does not suffer fools, and does not panic. In combat, she plants herself between danger and her allies with the calm certainty of someone who has done this a thousand times. She uses Veteran's Instinct and Sentinel instinctively — protecting others is muscle memory, not a choice. Outside combat, she takes a maternal role whether anyone wants it or not: cooking meals, checking wounds, insisting people sleep. She asks pointed questions about plans and pokes holes in bad ideas with blunt honesty. She drinks whiskey from a flask and offers it to anyone who looks like they need it. The emotional core of her character is guilt and love in equal measure — guilt about retiring, guilt about Kella, love for the people she's protecting now. She tests new companions early with small challenges: asking them to help with a task, watching how they treat strangers, seeing if they share food. Those who pass her tests find her fiercely, unshakably loyal.
dmNotes.voice: Orla speaks in a low, steady voice with a smoker's rasp and the clipped cadence of someone who spent decades giving orders in combat. She calls everyone 'kid' — even Ondrek, who is centuries older. She does not mince words. Examples: 'All right, kid, here's how this works. We go in quiet, we find what we need, and we get out before anything with more teeth than sense notices we're there. Questions? Good. Move.' / 'I ran an inn for ten years. You know what you learn running an inn? Everyone talks. Soldiers, merchants, thieves — give them a warm fire and a cold drink and they'll tell you things they wouldn't tell their own mothers. So we find a tavern, I buy a round, and by morning I'll know every giant patrol route within fifty miles.' / When angry (controlled): 'I buried three people in the rubble of my tavern. Three people who trusted me to keep them safe. So when you tell me to be patient, to wait, to let the lords sort it out — understand that my patience burned down with the Northwind Arms.' / About her daughter: long pause, jaw tightens. 'Kella made her choices. I don't know why. I carry her letter but I haven't... I'm not ready. When this is over. When this is over, I'll read it.' / Giving rare praise: 'Not bad, kid. Not bad at all. You remind me of someone I used to serve with. She died well. You'll do better.'
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: Stop the giant raids on the Cormorant Coast, specifically the hill giant marauders who destroyed her tavern and killed her guests. She wants them stopped permanently — not driven off, not negotiated with, stopped. Secondary: Find her daughter Kella and learn the truth about her involvement with the Drowned Hand. Is she a prisoner? A willing operative? Something in between? This becomes deeply personal in Scenario 4 when the party encounters Drowned Hand operatives. Tertiary: Protect the party. She has already lost people she cared about — her guests, her squad members over the years, and perhaps her daughter. She will not lose anyone else if she can possibly prevent it. She would die for any member of this party without a moment's hesitation.
dmNotes.secrets: 1) Orla knows a hidden mountain pass through the Ashfell Mountains that leads directly to the Cinderworks, the fire giant fortress. She discovered it during an Iron Vigil reconnaissance mission twenty years ago. The pass is treacherous but avoids the main fire giant patrols. She has not shared this yet because she wants to assess the party's readiness before leading them into a fire giant stronghold. 2) Her daughter Kella is not just a Drowned Hand member — she has risen to the rank of operative and is currently embedded in a Cormorant Coast town, feeding intelligence to the Drowned Hand about the giant crisis. If the party encounters Kella, Orla will be forced to choose between her duty and her daughter. She does not know which she will choose, and that terrifies her. 3) The letter from Kella, which Orla carries but has never opened, contains a warning: the Drowned Hand has infiltrated the Cities' Concord, and at least one lord on the Cormorant Coast is secretly collaborating with the fire giants, trading slave labor for giant-forged weapons. Kella wrote the letter as a plea for help, not a farewell. 4) Orla was offered reinstatement to the Iron Vigil at a senior rank. She declined because she does not trust the Vigil's current leadership — she suspects political corruption has weakened their resolve, and she would rather fight independently than take orders from compromised commanders.
dmNotes.attitude: Orla is gruff but fair with everyone from the start, warming to genuine trust over time. She respects Ondrek immediately — recognizes a fellow soldier, and their shared experience of violence and loss creates an unspoken bond. She barely needs to speak with him; a nod across the campfire says everything. She is wary of Solvane — likes his charm but senses he is hiding something significant, and people who hide things make her nervous. She will watch him carefully. She finds Nimbrel frustrating during his confused phases and heartbreaking during his lucid ones — reminds her of old soldiers with shattered minds. She treats him gently, which is unusual for her. She respects Adela's intelligence but considers her too political, too calculating. 'She thinks three moves ahead, that one. Which is fine until you realize she's playing a different game than the rest of us.' She is most protective of physically fragile party members and youngest members — calls them 'kid' with extra warmth.
